questions.q: What does passing DP-700 actually certify?
options: The Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate credential
General knowledge of all cloud data platforms
Certification as a Databricks administrator
A guarantee of a data engineering job
questions.explain: DP-700 is Microsoft's associate-level exam specifically for the Fabric Data Engineer role.

questions.q: How is the DP-700 exam scored?
options: On a scaled 1-1000 score, with a passing threshold set around 700
Pass/fail with no numeric score at all
As a percentage of questions answered in under a minute
By counting only the case-study questions
questions.explain: The certification's familiar '700' comes from the scaled score threshold, not the number of questions.

questions.q: What is a case-study section on DP-700?
options: A shared scenario about a fictional company's data platform, followed by several questions that all reference it
A single question with no context at all
A hands-on coding exercise graded live
An open-ended essay question
questions.explain: Case studies are the 'given this scenario, which of the following' style drilled starting in Lesson 31.

questions.q: Why does this chapter cite specific lesson numbers from earlier courses (like 'Fabric Lesson 21')?
options: Because this chapter reviews existing material rather than teaching new concepts, and the citation points back to where it was actually taught
Because those lessons are required prerequisites you must repeat before continuing
Because the numbering is arbitrary and has no real meaning
Because DP-700 requires proof you watched every prior lesson
questions.explain: Unlike every prior chapter in this track, this one drills and organizes what Courses 1-3 already covered.

questions.q: What does DP-700 explicitly NOT test?
options: Databricks, Snowflake, or dbt directly — it is Fabric-specific
Lakehouses and Warehouses
KQL and Eventstreams
Fabric notebooks and pipelines
questions.explain: DP-700 is scoped to Microsoft Fabric; other platforms from this track aren't part of the exam's official domains.
